title: REST APIs and JSON
subtitle: An API is a contract between programs: what to ask, in what shape, and what comes back.

rest.title: REST principles
rest.body: REST models an API as resources with URLs (/books, /books/7) and uses HTTP methods as verbs: GET read, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH change, DELETE remove. Stateless requests; standard status codes (201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found). Nouns in URLs, not verbs: DELETE /books/7, not /deleteBook.

json.title: JSON
json.body: JSON is text for objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null: {"id": 7, "title": "SICP", "tags": ["cs"]}. JSON.stringify / JSON.parse convert. Keys are quoted with double quotes; no trailing commas, no comments.

crud.title: A CRUD conversation
crud.body: Creating returns 201 and the new resource; reading returns 200; updating returns 200 or 204; deleting 204; a missing id 404.

idem.title: Idempotence and safety
idem.body: Safe methods (GET) change nothing. Idempotent methods (GET, PUT, DELETE) give the same final state if repeated; POST is not — retrying it may create two orders. Use an idempotency key for payments.
idem.steps: PUT /books/7 {title: "A"} sent twice. Final state is the same both times — it is idempotent.

auth.title: Authentication for APIs
auth.body: Clients send a credential with each request: an API key, or a bearer token in Authorization: Bearer …. OAuth 2.0 lets a user grant an app limited access without sharing a password; JWTs are signed, self-describing tokens (header.payload.signature) the server can verify without a lookup.

ver.title: Good API design
ver.body: Version the API (/v1/); paginate lists (?page=2&limit=20); return consistent error bodies; rate-limit; document with OpenAPI. Status 429 tells a client to slow down.
